papers.title_en: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
papers.authors: Zack Yu, Nicholas Lee, Minjae Lee, Lakshya Agarwal, Luca Manolache, Wonjun Kang, Matei Zaharia, Michael W. Mahoney, Kurt Keutzer, Sehoon Kim, Amir Gholami
papers.evidence: 通过筛选经验实现自我改进智能体的框架
papers.tldr: LLM 智能体在多轮任务中的失败来源多样，可能并非提示词缺陷，因此直接反思优化会引入噪声。GEPA-Curator 通过任务筛选与历史成功轨迹检索，为提示词优化器挑选可靠的学习经验。在 GoBrowse、ALFWorld、AppWorld 和 τ-bench 上，它用 Gemini 3.1 Pro 与 Claude Opus 5 作为优化器模型，性能持平或超过基线，较 GEPA 最高提升 20.7%，较 ACE 提升 21.2%。该工作强调经验筛选对自我改进智能体的重要性。
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. We argue that such failures may not provide useful learning signal, and may even be harmful; and thus it is essential to curate which tasks are provided to the prompt optimizer for better performance. We introduce GEPA-Curator, a framework that augments the prompt optimizer to select which agent experiences should shape prompt optimization. In particular, GEPA-Curator consists of two components: task curation, which filters out tasks that are likely to provide noisy or unreliable learning signals, and prior success retrieval, which selectively retrieves past successful trajectories for a task and provides them as additional context to the prompt optimizer. We evaluate GEPA-Curator on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and $τ$-bench, using both Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models. GEPA-Curator matches or exceeds the mean performance of both baselines, with gains of up to 20.7% over GEPA and 21.2% over ACE.

papers.title_en: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
papers.authors: Hau-Sing So, Daixian Liu, Weicai Long
papers.evidence: 分析自我改进智能体验收门控与冗余防护的侵蚀
papers.tldr: 自我改进的LLM智能体会改写自身harness，并以批量任务得分作为接受门。当多个防护措施重叠时，删除其中一个会被其余措施掩盖，门只看任务成功率，导致冗余防护在无人察觉中流失。作者在两种环境中测量四种防护的全部子集，运行411次改进循环和十种门规则，发现配对显著性检验只拦住偶然通过，挡不住真正提升成功率的删除；更大的评估批次反而让门删除更便宜的防护。该工作揭示了接受门会系统性侵蚀安全深度，并提出冻结安全文本或单层审计可保留冗余。
papers.abstract_en: Self-improving LLM agents edit their own harness, the prompts and rules around a fixed model, and keep an edit only if an acceptance gate scores it higher on a batch of tasks. Such a gate sees what the harness does under the current model, not what it would still prevent if one safeguard failed. When safeguards overlap, deleting one is masked: the others still block the harm, so the gate decides on task success alone and redundancy erodes unseen. We measure harm for every subset of four written safeguards in two agent environments and run 411 improvement loops under ten gate rules, mostly as controlled deletion experiments, plus three runs of the GEPA optimizer. A deletion behind another working safeguard adds almost no observable harm. A paired significance test blocks deletions that pass by chance but not deletions that genuinely raise task success, and a larger evaluation batch lets it delete cheaper safeguards: at the same cost, 20-task batches kept every harness protected while 40-task batches lost all six. Large harm audits prevent exposure but not the loss of depth, which turns into harm when the harness is reused with a weaker model. GEPA kept every safety rule verbatim, yet two of its three final harnesses misused credentials under a weaker model. A statistical model frozen before the runs predicts where each gate's protection breaks as safeguard cost and batch size change, and freezing safety text or auditing one-layer ablations preserves depth.

papers.title_en: Compile Away Uncertainty: Self-Evolving Agent Skills via Programmatic Compilation
papers.authors: Chengyu Yang, Yunxiang Zheng, Zongzheng Li, Jiamei Li, Boxun Lan, Xiaoyu Liu, Xiaoyu Zhang, Xiaohong Chen, Ming Hu
papers.evidence: 自我演化智能体技能积累并精炼可复用知识
papers.tldr: 自进化智能体技能多以文本表示并依赖LLM反复推理执行，带来可避免的不确定性。SkillCompiler将程序化编译引入技能演化：按可执行性分解技能，构建混合技能骨架，把明确操作编译为经验证程序，并复用程序资产。在五个基准和六类模型上，它稳定优于现有方法，任务性能最高提升32.33%。该工作以确定性、可验证的程序执行降低推理依赖，促进可执行知识积累。
papers.abstract_en: Self-evolving agent skills enable AI agents to accumulate and refine reusable procedural knowledge from interaction experience without updating model parameters. However, since such skills are typically represented as textual documents and executed through LLM reasoning, even previously learned procedures must be repeatedly interpreted and regenerated, introducing avoidable uncertainty into every execution. In contrast, program execution is deterministic and independently verifiable. Intuitively, transforming well-specified operations into executable programs can reduce reliance on LLM reasoning and, consequently, reduce execution uncertainty. Motivated by this intuition, we introduce SKillCompiler, a self-evolving skill framework that integrates programmatic compilation into the skill evolution process. Specifically, SkillCompiler adopts an executability-aware skill compilation strategy that decomposes skills into fine-grained operations, analyzes their executability, and constructs hybrid skill skeletons that retain LLM reasoning for context-dependent operations while compiling well-specified ones into validated programs. To avoid redundant program synthesis and enable executable knowledge to accumulate across evolving skills, we further design a program asset reuse mechanism that organizes validated programs as reusable assets, retrieves existing implementations whenever applicable, and synthesizes and verifies new programs only when necessary. Extensive experiments on five benchmarks and six model families demonstrate that SkillCompiler consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to 32.33\% improvement in task performance.
